title: Just-In-Time Learning
hook: You don't need another course. You need a real problem in front of you.
statement: Learn skills right when you need them, not months ahead just in case.
explainer: Stuff you learn for someday mostly fades before someday shows up. Learn it in the middle of the real job and it sticks, because you used it right away.
sop: Name the specific problem in front of you right now.
Find the minimum info you need to solve just that.
Score the Contextual Relevance of what you're learning from 1 to 10.
Use it right away on the real thing, not a practice run.
Go deeper only when the next real need shows up.
equation_example: Score Contextual Relevance from 1 to 10. Learning mid-task is a 9, so Retention is high. Learning for someday is a 2, so most of it's gone before you need it. Higher relevance means it sticks. Lower means it evaporates.
question: Write down one thing you've been preparing to learn, and the real task where you could learn it this week.
closing_statement: Knowledge sticks when you need it, not before.
caption:
Principle Nº 232: Just-In-Time Learning

You don't need another course. You need a real problem in front of you.

Learn skills right when you need them, not months ahead just in case.

Your turn: Write down one thing you've been preparing to learn, and the real task where you could learn it this week.
